prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core pitch: The Conservatives argue the economy has stabilised (inflation down, growth and real wages up) and promise a “secure future” built on lower immigration, lower taxes and protected pensions, contrasting this with Labour’s alleged risks of higher taxes and weaker border/defence policies.

Key pledges:
- Tax and pensions: Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main self‑employed NI next Parliament; Triple Lock Plus so both State Pension and pensioner tax‑free allowance rise by earnings, inflation or 2.5%; no rises in income tax or VAT. Child Benefit to a household test with taper from £120k–£160k. 30 hours’ free childcare from 9 months old.
- Economy and business: Keep debt falling and borrowing under 3% in year 5; no rise in corporation tax; extend full expensing (including to leasing when affordable); 10‑point SME plan (rates relief, prompt payment, finance access, less reporting). Invest HS2 savings in regional transport; nationwide gigabit/5G; public R&D to £22bn; AI compute and advanced manufacturing push. Pursue FTAs (CPTPP implementation; India, GCC) and Brexit‑led deregulation. Cut Whitehall size, consultants, and boost productivity via digital/AI.
- Education and youth: Advanced British Standard (broader post‑16; English and maths to 18); 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by curbing poor‑value degrees; statutory mobile‑phone bans in schools; attendance drive; expand SEND places. Mandatory National Service at 18 (competitive paid military/cyber year or 25 days civic service).
- Borders and migration: Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; veterans’ bill and support. Monthly Rwanda removal flights; legal annual migration cap on work/family visas that falls each year and is voted by Parliament; tighter salary thresholds; asylum rules reform and more returns deals.
- NHS and social care: Real‑terms annual NHS funding rises; recruit 92,000 nurses and 28,000 doctors; Pharmacy First; 250 GP surgery builds/modernisations; 50 more Community Diagnostic Centres; dental recovery plan with NHS service requirement for new dentists. £3.4bn tech programme (NHS App as single front door, AI diagnostics, federated data platform) to lift productivity. Women’s health strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; implement Cass Review; protect single‑sex spaces.
- Crime and justice: 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing and tougher community sentences; new offences (spiking, deepfakes); harsher sentences for serious/sexual offences and domestic murders; four new prisons; faster removals of foreign offenders; anti‑fraud crackdown; tighter protest rules and extremism definition.
- Energy and net zero: Net zero 2050 with a “pragmatic” path—annual North Sea licensing, new gas plants for security, treble offshore wind, carbon capture clusters, scale nuclear (two SMR fleets; Wylfa large plant), no new green levies, maintain price cap, energy‑efficiency vouchers, protect best farmland from solar; no fracking; import carbon pricing by 2027.
- Housing: 1.6m homes—brownfield fast‑track, urban densification, nutrient neutrality reform; permanent FTB stamp duty threshold at £425k; new Help to Buy; renter reform (end s21 with court changes); complete leasehold reform; CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants; social housing “local/UK connection” tests and ASB evictions.
- Communities, transport and drivers: Long‑Term Plan for Towns, Shared Prosperity Fund extension, more Freeports/Investment Zones; Backing Drivers Bill (ban road pricing, reverse London ULEZ expansion, local referendums for LTNs/20mph); £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament; Rail Reform Bill to create Great British Railways.
- Rural, farming, fisheries, environment: Farming budget up £1bn (inflation‑linked); legal food security target; tapered seasonal visas and automation push; replicate £100m Seafood Fund; flood‑defence funding maintained; tougher water regulation and river recovery; tree/peat restoration; more access to nature without universal Right to Roam.
- Equality, sex and gender: Clarify Equality Act that “sex” means biological sex; single legal sex standard UK‑wide; protect women’s sport/spaces; statutory school guidance on gender‑questioning children; cautious approach on conversion therapy legislation.
- Union and foreign policy: Protect the UK internal market; direct levelling‑up funds across Scotland, Wales, NI; implement Windsor Framework; global leadership on defence, sanctions, and trade.
